stories.headline: Marvell agrees to buy optics maker Lumentum in $115B all-stock deal to challenge Broadcom

key_facts.fact: Marvell and Lumentum announced on November 2, 2026 a definitive agreement for Marvell to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum.
key_facts.excerpt: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL) and Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement for Marvell to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction... The transaction has an implied enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum

key_facts.fact: Lumentum holders get 4.500 Marvell shares per share, about $1,132 per share, a ~23.9% premium to the October 28 unaffected close; Marvell holders will own ~67% of the combined company and Lumentum holders ~33%.
key_facts.excerpt: a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock... approximately $1,132 per share of Lumentum common stock and a premium of approximately 23.9% based on each company's unaffected closing share price as of October 28, 2026... current Marvell stockholders will own approximately 67%... Lumentum stockholders will own approximately 33%.

key_facts.fact: The companies expect more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies, a combined total addressable market of $550 billion, and accretion to Marvell's non-GAAP EPS in year one after closing.
key_facts.excerpt: Expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion... line of sight to more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies, and is expected to be accretive to Marvell non-GAAP earnings per share in year one post-close

key_facts.fact: Matt Murphy stays chairman and CEO; three Lumentum directors, including CEO Michael Hurlston, join Marvell's board; closing is expected in the first half of calendar 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: Matt Murphy will continue as Chairman and CEO of the combined company. As part of the transaction, three members of Lumentum's Board of Directors, including Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, will join Marvell's Board... expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028

key_facts.fact: The merger agreement was signed on November 1, 2026, per Marvell's 8-K filing, and requires HSR antitrust clearance and other regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: On November 1, 2026, Marvell Technology, Inc.... entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") with Lumentum Holdings Inc.... (c) the expiration or termination of any waiting period applicable to the Merger under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act

key_facts.fact: Reuters frames the deal as Marvell stepping up its challenge to larger rival Broadcom; Nvidia invested $2 billion each in Marvell and Lumentum earlier in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: as the custom chipmaker steps up its challenge to larger rival Broadcom amid an AI spending boom... AI chip giant Nvidia invested $2 billion each in Marvell and Lumentum earlier this year.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg calls it one of the biggest tech tie-ups ever.
key_facts.excerpt: Marvell Technology Inc. has reached a deal to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings Inc. at an enterprise value of $115 billion, one of the biggest tech tie-ups ever

stories.headline: Google's Suncatcher satellite runs Gemma 4 on a TPU in orbit; its energy chief says space DCs cost up to 100x

key_facts.fact: Google said on October 30, 2026 that its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, launched October 1, produced the first-ever AI response from a data-center-class TPU in orbit, running its Gemma 4 open model.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher... This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit... we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model

key_facts.fact: Google will next test how the TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation, ahead of a planned pair of interconnected satellites in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.

key_facts.fact: The satellite carries four TPUs and generates up to 1 kilowatt, so it can run only one TPU at a time for about 20 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellite holds four TPUs and generates up to 1 kilowatt of power... Because of that power limit, it can run only one TPU at a time, for about 20 minutes.

key_facts.fact: The spacecraft was built by Planet Labs.
key_facts.excerpt: Spacecraft built by Planet Labs demonstrates Google's data-center processor in orbit

key_facts.fact: By Google's own calculations, launch costs would need to fall to about $200/kg for amortized orbital costs to be comparable to terrestrial data-center electricity spending.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Google's calculations, if the cost of getting a satellite into low Earth orbit can be brought down to $200/kg, the launch cost amortized over the satellite's useful life (~$810–7,500/kW/year) could be comparable to current electricity spending for terrestrial datacenters in the US (~$570–3,000/kW/year).

key_facts.fact: Google's head of data center energy, Amanda Peterson Corio, said space data centers could cost up to 100 times as much as those on Earth: "Let's explore all the terrestrial options before we go extraterrestrial."
key_facts.excerpt: Data centers in space could cost up to 100 times as much as those on Earth, Google's head of data center energy said this week... "Let's explore all the terrestrial options before we go extraterrestrial," Amanda Peterson Corio said at The Information's WTF summit

key_facts.fact: Peterson Corio said US power supply is sufficient and that the real bottleneck is grid-interconnection approvals and studies.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's data center energy head says space data centers cost up to 100x more than Earth-based ones, and US power supply is sufficient but permits are slow

stories.headline: Meta built a humanoid robot prototype, 'Max', with China's Fourier and is working on a second version

key_facts.fact: Meta developed a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics startup Fourier and is already working on a second version, The Information reported on Saturday, October 31.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) has developed a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese robotics startup Fourier and is already working on a second version, The Information reported on Saturday

key_facts.fact: The prototype, internally named Max, weighs about 106 pounds, stands about 1.5 meters tall, was built in roughly three months, and runs on Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip with five-fingered hands and a face-mimicking display.
key_facts.excerpt: The prototype, internally named Max, weighs about 106 pounds and was built by the two companies in roughly three months... Standing around 1.5 metres tall, the robot uses Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip and features a display capable of mimicking facial expressions, built-in speakers and five-fingered hands

key_facts.fact: Meta's VP of product for robotics, Li-Chen Miller, spent almost two months at Fourier's Shanghai factory; Max was shown to employees at an internal robotics summit in late August.
key_facts.excerpt: the company's vice president of product for robotics, Li-Chen Miller, spending almost two months at the startup's Shanghai factory, the report said. Max was demonstrated to some Meta employees at an internal robotics summit in late August.

key_facts.fact: Work on Max 2 began in September, with a redesigned torso, better hands, a projector and extra sensors for stairs.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies began developing a second prototype, Max 2, in September. The updated version is expected to feature a redesigned torso, improved hands for handling objects, a projector and additional sensors to help it navigate stairs

key_facts.fact: Meta sees humanoids as a physical extension of its Muse AI agent, but told The Information the Fourier work is internal research with no plans to sell the units.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta sees humanoid robots as a potential physical extension of its Muse AI agent... However, Meta told The Information that its work with Fourier was focused on internal research and experimentation and that it had no plans to sell the units.

stories.headline: South Korea's October chip exports jump 259% to $56.4B; Kioxia sinks 16% as memory stocks split

key_facts.fact: South Korea's semiconductor exports rose 259.4% year on year to $56.44 billion in October, above $50 billion for a second straight month, the trade ministry said on November 1.
key_facts.excerpt: In IT, semiconductor exports rose 259.4 percent to $56.44 billion, exceeding $50.0 billion for a second consecutive month. Export unit prices and volumes remained high as global big tech companies continued capital investment

key_facts.fact: Total exports rose 93.7% to a record-for-October $115.28 billion, with a $42.5 billion trade surplus; January-October exports topped $900 billion for the first time and the ministry expects $1 trillion for the year in November.
key_facts.excerpt: in October 2026, Korea's exports rose 93.7 percent year-on-year to USD 115.28 billion... resulting in a trade surplus of $42.50 billion... Cumulative exports from January to October 2026 reached $930.0 billion... annual exports are now set to reach $1 trillion in November.

key_facts.fact: Memory chip exports surged 360.5% to $50.14 billion, 88.8% of chip exports; chips were 49% of all Korean exports, up from 26.4% a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: 메모리반도체 수출은 501억4000만달러로 360.5% 급증했다. 전체 반도체 수출의 88.8%에 해당한다... 전체 수출의 49.0%로 지난해 10월 26.4%에서 22.6%p 높아졌다.

key_facts.fact: Computer exports, mostly server SSDs, rose 496.6% to $5.85 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: 컴퓨터 수출은 58억5000만달러로 496.6% 증가했고, 이 가운데 SSD가 56억4000만달러를 차지했다.

key_facts.fact: On November 2 Samsung Electronics rose 1.78% and SK hynix 3.81% after early losses, while Japan's Kioxia plunged 15.78% after its fourth-quarter profit outlook missed expectations.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics gained 1.78 percent to 229,000 won, while SK hynix advanced 3.81 percent to 1,472,000 won after both chipmakers recovered from early losses... Kioxia plunged 15.78 percent to 11,345 yen after its profit outlook for the fourth quarter fell short of market expectations

key_facts.fact: The Asian session followed a Friday US selloff in which the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 7.20%.
key_facts.excerpt: another selloff in U.S. tech stocks on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 2.86 percent and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping 7.20 percent

stories.headline: Korea's Lee pitches 21.3T won ($16B) for chips, physical AI and AI data centers, nearly double 2026

key_facts.fact: In a budget speech to the National Assembly on November 2, President Lee Jae Myung said the government will invest 21.3 trillion won (~$16 billion), nearly twice this year's amount, in AI and three megaprojects: semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: "We will invest 21.3 trillion won (€14.3 billion, $15.97 billion), nearly twice this year's amount, in AI and the three megaprojects of semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centres," Lee said on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The plan includes 2 trillion won to expand chip production capacity (earlier start of fabs near Seoul and a southwestern cluster), 500 billion won for physical-AI field trials, 2.1 trillion won for power, water and industrial-park infrastructure, and 4.7 trillion won for frontier AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposal earmarks 2 trillion won to expand semiconductor production capacity, including accelerating chip-fabrication plants near Seoul and developing a southwestern industrial cluster. Another 4.7 trillion won will support frontier AI development... 500 billion won for physical AI trials... 2.1 trillion won for power, water and industrial infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Lee also announced a new special account to strengthen semiconductor industry competitiveness.
key_facts.excerpt: 반도체산업 경쟁력 강화 특별회계 신설로 안정적 투자 기반을 마련하고, 수도권 팹의 조기 가동과 서남권 클러스터 구축 등 생산기반 확충에 2조 원을 투자하겠다

key_facts.fact: The total 2027 budget is a record 820.9 trillion won, up 12.8%, made possible by expected tax revenue from record profits at Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.
key_facts.excerpt: The sharp increase in the 2027 budget was made possible by expectations of higher tax revenue amid record high profits at semiconductor giants, including Samsung Electronics Co. and SK hynix Inc., fueled by the AI boom

key_facts.fact: Lee asked lawmakers to pass the budget by the December 2 statutory deadline; the opposition People Power Party has questioned the fund financed by chip-boom tax windfalls.
key_facts.excerpt: as the National Assembly began reviewing the spending proposal ahead of the Dec. 2 passage deadline... The main opposition People Power Party has questioned its fiscal implications and urged the government to use more of the windfall to reduce national debt.

stories.headline: Altman meets 50 Samsung executives and SK's Chey in Korea, with OpenAI's chip head in tow

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met about 50 Samsung Group executives from electronics, finance and biotech affiliates in Yongin on Saturday, October 31, on an unannounced visit to South Korea, Samsung said.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman made an unannounced visit to South Korea over the weekend, meeting with Samsung executives... Samsung said Saturday that Altman met with around 50 executives from its affiliates spanning electronics, finance and biotechnology in Yongin

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the talks aimed to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group's top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify.

key_facts.fact: Altman also reportedly lunched with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won with SK Hynix and SK Telecom executives present; SK Hynix said it could not confirm the meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman also met with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won over lunch Saturday, with senior executives from SK Hynix and SK Telecom in attendance, according to South Korean media reports... SK Hynix told CNBC it was unable to confirm the reported meeting.

key_facts.fact: Richard Ho, OpenAI's VP in charge of in-house AI chip development, accompanied Altman; industry sources say OpenAI's in-house accelerator, Jalapeño, is expected to use Samsung's HBM4.
key_facts.excerpt: Richard Ho, OpenAI's vice president in charge of in-house AI chip development, accompanied Altman on the trip... OpenAI's in-house AI accelerator, Jalapeño, is expected to carry Samsung Electronics' next-generation high-bandwidth memory, HBM4, according to industry sources.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's Commercial Times reports OpenAI's first-generation ASIC uses TSMC 3nm and the second generation is planned on TSMC's A16 process.
key_facts.excerpt: Commercial Times reports, citing supply chain sources, that OpenAI's first-generation ASIC uses TSMC's 3nm process, while its second-generation chip is reportedly planned to adopt A16

stories.headline: Trump backs Jensen Huang over spy report; Singapore denies probing Alice Huang, Megaspeed probe ongoing

key_facts.fact: On October 31 President Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang "brilliant" and said the US would look "very closely" at reports he was targeted by a Chinese spy plot.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump voiced on Oct 31 his support for the "brilliant" head of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang, after a report that he was targeted by a Chinese spy plot. Trump said the US was looking "very closely" at the issue.

key_facts.fact: Asked whether he would keep Huang as an adviser, Trump said: "I would like to say yes... unless we find out something to the contrary."
key_facts.excerpt: Asked if he would retain Huang as an adviser, he said: "I would like to say yes. I mean, unless we find out something to the contrary, I've always found Jensen Huang to be very above board."

key_facts.fact: Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said on October 31 that no investigations were conducted into Megaspeed-linked executive Alice Huang over alleged ties to Jensen Huang or Chinese intelligence, disputing a Wall Street Journal report.
key_facts.excerpt: We would like to make clear that neither the Singapore Government nor its officials said this. And there were no such investigations conducted in respect of Alice Huang.

key_facts.fact: Singapore police confirmed that investigations into Megaspeed itself are ongoing, and noted Singapore has charged four individuals and four companies since February 2025 for fraud on server suppliers.
key_facts.excerpt: Investigations into Megaspeed are ongoing. We are unable to comment further at this juncture... Singapore has charged four individuals and four companies in Court between Feb 2025 and Jul 2026 for committing fraud on suppliers of servers

key_facts.fact: Singapore said it does not implement unilateral foreign export controls but does not condone companies using their Singapore association to circumvent them.
key_facts.excerpt: Singapore does not implement unilateral export controls imposed by foreign jurisdictions. At the same time, Singapore does not condone businesses deliberately using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate other countries' export controls.
